newsitem.title: UK: Pentland enters 1997 with record order book.
newsitem.headline: Pentland enters 1997 with record order book.

text.p: British clothing company Pentland Group Plc said on Tuesday it entered 1997 with record order books in many of its businesses.

In a statement attached to the company's 1996 results chairman Stephen Rubin said, "We enter 1997 with record order books in many of our businesses and expect trading improvements in our continuing businesses."
Earlier Pentland reported a 13 percent increase in pre-tax profits, excluding exceptional items to 36.6 million stg.

The pre-tax profit and operating profit exclude exceptional charges of 40.4 million, mainly relating to the sale of Woods Industries -- an American maker of electrical accessories sold in December for 27 million.

Profits from the companies footwear, clothing and sports division rose 3.2 million stg to 21.3 million in the year to December 31, 1996 while consumer products grew profits 2.1 million stg to 9.0 million.

Kickers, one of Britain's leading brands of leisure footwear for young adults, increased sales by more than 60 percent and the order book for the first half of 1997 was also well up, said the company.

But after taking into account a poor performance by its Italian distribution company Olympico and the effect of buying football maker Mitre, there was a small decline in profit from the sports and outdoor division.
The company said its Speedo swimwear brand was worn by 76 percent of all Olympic medals in the pool at the Atlanta games, helping to give the brand its greatest ever international media exposure.

After a strategic review Pentland has decided to focus on the sports, leisure and fashion markets, to complete its re-focusing it plans to sell domestic electrical appliance company Holmes Products division.
Pentland shares were up 4-1/2p at 108-1/2p in early trade.
